parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Karakhanid [script needed] (basïnč, “pressure; tyranny”), from Proto-Turkic *bas- (“to press”), equivalent to bas- (“to press, to put one's foot on”) + -ın + -ç. Compare also Turkmen basyş, Southern Altai базыш (bazïš), Uyghur بېسىم (bësim), Uzbek bosim, Kyrgyz басым (basım),
Learned borrowing from Karakhanid اِكِذْماكْ (ʾikiḏmʾk /⁠igiḏmek⁠/, “to feed”), introduced during 1930's, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *igid- (“to feed”).

Learned borrowing from Karakhanid [script needed] (kīp), from Proto-Turkic *kēp (“form, image, example”). The sense mood is a semantic loan from Arabic صيغة (ṣīḡa, “form”), coined by Hüseyin Hüsâmeddin Yasar in 1926 and popularized during the language reform and displaced siga, sıyga. Doublet of gib

Derived from Karakhanid تَرِیـ (tarï-, “to cultivate”) with the suffix -ım (“deverbal nominal”), however the verb "*tarımak" does not exist in Turkish. Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *tarï-. Coined by Turkish Language Association in 1935 to replace Arabic-derived ziraat.
Learned borrowing from Karakhanid ﻳﻨﺖ (yanut) made in the time of the Language reform, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yan- (“to turn back”). Cognate with Uyghur يانوت (yanot), Salar yanıt.
